fact: Djibouti's government launched the US$8m EU-financed 'E-SKILLS' project to develop the digital abilities of at least 3,000 youths and women by 2029, per Djibouti News Agency via Ecofin.
Djibouti's government launched the EU-funded E-SKILLS programme to train at least 3,000 youths and women in digital skills by 2029.
Djibouti's Ministry of Digital Economy and the EU launched the E-SKILLS project, implemented by Expertise France, to train over 3,000 young people and women in digital skills by 2029.

The government launched a feasibility study (statement of 13 May 2026) for Digital Houses in five inland regions under the E-SKILLS programme, which aims to train at least 3,000 young people and women by 2029 for about EUR 7 million.

The Ministry of Digital Economy and Innovation launched work on École 42 Djibouti, a project-based coding school for young people in software development, cybersecurity and data, with EU E-Skills programme and Expertise France support, per Tech Review Africa.
The European Commission's Djibouti partnership page lists support to build digital skills, including citizens' digital literacy, professional ICT training and recognised certifications.
